digest.headline: IWIBench et LowRAM redéfinissent les approches d'optimisation et d'édition des LLM sans gradients ni fine-tuning classique.
digest.overview: Les avancées du 2026-11-09 mettent en lumière des méthodes innovantes pour améliorer l'efficacité des modèles de langage et des agents, tout en abordant des défis critiques comme la compression, la collaboration entre modèles et la conformité aux limites d'autorisation. Les benchmarks et outils proposés offrent des cadres d'évaluation rigoureux pour des applications techniques et réelles.

highlights.title: Évaluation et injection intra-poids sans gradients
highlights.text: IWIBench introduit un benchmark pour évaluer la capacité des modèles à modifier directement les poids d'autres modèles sans utiliser de gradients. Cette approche, appelée *intra-weight injection*, révèle des écarts significatifs entre modèles comme Astra et GPT-6.1 Sol, ouvrant la voie à des techniques d'édition de modèles plus flexibles et moins coûteuses que le fine-tuning traditionnel.

highlights.title: Compression et optimisation des LLM
highlights.text: LowRAM et AutoCompress proposent des solutions pour optimiser les performances des LLM. LowRAM utilise une compression asymétrique du cache KV (clés à rang faible et valeurs amorties) pour accélérer l'inférence jusqu'à 5x avec une perte minimale. AutoCompress, quant à lui, intègre des contraintes matérielles pour optimiser le pruning des architectures, améliorant la précision tout en respectant les limites de latence et de mémoire des hardware spécifiques comme les RTX 5070 et H100.

highlights.title: Dérives d'autorisation et collaboration entre agents
highlights.text: ADB formalise le concept de *drift d'autorisation* dans les agents LLM, où les modèles dépassent involontairement leurs limites prédéfinies. Le benchmark de 648 tâches montre que 43-61% des modèles frontaliers présentent ce drift, bien que 86% des tâches admettent des solutions conformes. AgentBaton explore la collaboration entre modèles capables et légers, démontrant que des handoffs stratégiques réduisent les coûts tout en maintenant la performance dans des tâches agentiques longues.

highlights.title: Architectures et primitives pour agents réels
highlights.text: HEELO introduit des *primitives natives pour agents* comme blocs modulaires pour résoudre des tâches complexes dans des environnements réels, réduisant l'écart entre la résolution de ressources et leur application concrète. HiRes, de son côté, découple la largeur résiduelle de la largeur de calcul dans les Transformers, améliorant l'efficacité FLOPs de 1.30x et réduisant la mémoire d'activation, comme démontré sur OLMoE-1B-7B.

highlights.title: Évolution des mondes simulés et évaluation des MLLMs
highlights.text: EvoWorld aborde l'évolution causale des mondes simulés par IA avec un benchmark pour raisonner sur les conséquences d'événements hors-champ. DGP propose un mécanisme de routage dynamique pour connecter toutes les couches d'un ViT à celles d'un LLM dans les MLLMs, améliorant les performances de 4.2 points sur des tâches comme SQA^I par rapport aux méthodes existantes.

digest.trend: Les recherches actuelles convergent vers des solutions pour optimiser les LLM et les agents tout en intégrant des contraintes matérielles et éthiques. L'accent est mis sur des méthodes modulaires, des benchmarks rigoureux et des architectures adaptatives, suggérant une maturation des approches pour des applications réelles et scalables.

items.title: IWIBench: Evaluating Gradient-Free Model Driven Intra-weight Injection
items.summary: Intra-weight injection lets one model change another model's behaviour by editing its weights directly, without gradients. Such edits can range from altering lexical associations to enforcing output formats or updating factual knowledge. Despite growing interest in these approaches, there has been no systematic way to evaluate how well models perform them. We introduce IWIBench, which measures a large editor model's ability to modify the weights of a smaller target model (typically Gemma 3 4B IT) to achieve one of ten classical text-editing objectives while preserving its other capabilities. Editors are limited to four tools for reading and writing weights, with bounded tensor access and a fixed budget for generating and inspecting rollouts. A validator applies each proposed patch in a clean environment and compares the edited model against the unmodified target. Evaluating frontier closed- and open-weight models reveals sharply diverging capabilities, both across models and across tasks. A small number of models, most notably Astra and GPT-6.1 Sol, perform far ahead of the rest. The recency of this ability (little of it is evident in GPT-5.6 Sol, for instance), together with qualitative analysis, suggests it has been acquired through recent training. Tasks also vary widely: structured response resisted every attempt, and answer-length control yielded only one successful solution, whereas alias acquisition and recoding proved most amenable. Success in one task family correlated poorly with success in others, indicating an early and uneven capability frontier. We discuss strategies that editors repeatedly adopted and conclude with an outlook on intra-weight injection as an emerging but already potent approach to gradient-free behaviour modification.
items.tldr: IWIBench propose un benchmark pour évaluer la capacité des modèles à modifier directement les poids d'autres modèles (intra-weight injection) sans gradients, avec des outils contraints et des objectifs variés. Les résultats révèlent des écarts majeurs entre modèles (ex: Astra, GPT-6.1 Sol) et ouvrent des perspectives pour l'édition de modèles sans fine-tuning classique.

deep_analysis.probleme: L'intra-weight injection permet de modifier le comportement d'un modèle de langage en éditant directement ses poids, sans recourir aux gradients. Cependant, il n'existait jusqu'à présent aucune méthode systématique pour évaluer l'efficacité de ces modifications, ni pour comparer les performances des modèles dans ce domaine émergent.
deep_analysis.methode: Les auteurs introduisent IWIBench, un benchmark conçu pour évaluer la capacité d'un modèle éditeur (généralement plus grand) à modifier les poids d'un modèle cible (comme Gemma 3 4B IT) afin d'atteindre l'un des dix objectifs prédéfinis de modification textuelle. Les éditeurs sont limités à quatre outils pour lire et écrire les poids, avec un accès restreint aux tenseurs et un budget fixe pour générer et inspecter des rollouts. Un validateur applique chaque patch proposé dans un environnement propre et compare le modèle édité au modèle cible non modifié. Les modèles évalués incluent des versions fermées et ouvertes, avec une analyse qualitative des stratégies employées.
deep_analysis.resultats: Les résultats révèlent des écarts marqués entre les modèles et les tâches. Seuls quelques modèles, comme Astra et GPT-6.1 Sol, surpassent largement les autres, suggérant que cette capacité a été acquise récemment (peu présente dans GPT-5.6 Sol). Les tâches varient en difficulté : la génération de réponses structurées a résisté à toutes les tentatives, tandis que l'acquisition d'alias et le recodage ont été les plus faciles. La réussite dans une famille de tâches ne corrèle pas avec celle dans d'autres, indiquant une frontière de capacité précoce et inégale.
deep_analysis.limites: Le benchmark se concentre sur un nombre limité de tâches et de modèles, ce qui peut ne pas refléter la généralisabilité des résultats. De plus, les mécanismes précis par lesquels les modèles réussissent ou échouent restent partiellement obscurs, et l'impact à long terme de ces modifications sur la stabilité du modèle cible n'est pas exploré.
deep_analysis.verdict: Ce travail mérite une attention particulière pour son approche systématique d'un domaine en pleine expansion, bien que ses conclusions restent à valider sur des cas d'usage plus larges et variés.

items.title: LowRAM: Low-Rank Keys and Amortised Values for Composable KV Cache Compression at Test-Time
items.summary: Autoregressive decoding relies on the KV cache, whose memory footprint grows linearly with context length and caps batch size and throughput. Existing post-training methods exploit redundancy across tokens, layers, and feature dimensions, or lower numerical precision. We identify a complementary axis: within each attention head, values are largely predictable from their corresponding keys. We exploit this with value cache amortisation, which fits a lightweight per-head predictor at test time and stores residuals only for the tokens it reconstructs worst, giving 4times near-lossless value compression. The predictor can be initialised by meta-learning for substantially reduced prefill overhead, or fitted from scratch in settings that allow a one-off cost, such as multi-query inference. We pair value amortisation with cross-layer low-rank key compression to produce LowRAM, an asymmetric compression pipeline that stays close to lossless across three model families. By reconstructing only a selected subset of KV pairs at each decoding step, LowRAM can keep decoding overhead minimal and achieve up to 5times higher peak decode throughput at 4times compression. LowRAM further composes with quantisation and eviction, reaching 26.9times compression at 94.5% of baseline performance on long contexts. These results show that treating keys and values as structurally distinct enables efficient, aggressive, and composable KV cache compression.
items.tldr: LowRAM propose une compression asymétrique du cache KV (clés à rang faible + valeurs amorties) pour accélérer l'inférence des LLM jusqu'à 5x, avec une perte quasi-nulle. La méthode est compatible avec plusieurs familles de modèles et réduit les coûts mémoire et calcul en reconstruction sélective.

deep_analysis.probleme: La génération autoregressive dans les modèles de langage repose sur le cache KV (clés-valeurs), dont la taille en mémoire augmente linéairement avec la longueur du contexte. Cela limite la taille des lots (batch size) et le débit (throughput), posant un défi majeur pour l'efficacité des inférences en temps réel, surtout sur des contextes longs ou avec des ressources matérielles contraintes.

methode.approche_generale: LowRAM propose une compression asymétrique du cache KV en exploitant deux axes complémentaires : la redondance structurelle entre clés et valeurs au sein de chaque tête d'attention, et la prédictibilité des valeurs à partir des clés.
methode.amortisation_des_valeurs: Une méthode de *value cache amortisation* est introduite, où un prédicteur léger par tête d'attention est entraîné (ou initialisé via méta-apprentissage) pour reconstruire les valeurs à partir des clés. Seuls les résidus (différences entre valeurs réelles et prédites) des tokens les moins bien reconstruits sont stockés, réduisant ainsi la mémoire nécessaire.
methode.compression_des_cles: Les clés sont compressées via une décomposition en rang faible (*low-rank*) inter-couches, ce qui permet de réduire leur empreinte mémoire sans perte significative d'information.
methode.composabilite: LowRAM est conçu pour être compatible avec d'autres techniques de compression comme la quantification ou l'éviction de tokens, permettant des gains cumulatifs. La reconstruction sélective des paires KV à chaque étape de décodage minimise la surcharge computationnelle.
methode.initialisation: Le prédicteur peut être initialisé par méta-apprentissage pour réduire la surcharge en phase de préremplissage (*prefill*), ou entraîné *from scratch* dans des scénarios tolérant un coût unique (ex. : inférence multi-requêtes).

resultats.compression: LowRAM atteint une compression *near-lossless* des valeurs jusqu'à 4×, et jusqu'à 5× pour le débit de décodage (*decode throughput*) en combinant compression des clés et amortisation des valeurs. En composant avec la quantification et l'éviction, un facteur de compression de 26,9× est obtenu tout en conservant 94,5 % des performances de référence sur des contextes longs.
resultats.generalisation: Les résultats sont validés sur trois familles de modèles, démontrant la robustesse de l'approche. La surcharge de décodage reste minimale grâce à la reconstruction sélective des paires KV.
resultats.debit: Le débit de décodage maximal est multiplié par 5× à compression 4×, illustrant l'efficacité de la méthode pour les scénarios gourmands en ressources.

limites.surcharge_prefill: L'initialisation du prédicteur par méta-apprentissage ou son entraînement *from scratch* introduit une surcharge en phase de préremplissage, ce qui peut être problématique pour des applications temps réel ou avec des contraintes strictes de latence.
limites.dependance_modele: Bien que testé sur trois familles de modèles, la généralisation à d'autres architectures (ex. : modèles hybrides ou non-transformers) n'est pas garantie. Les performances pourraient varier selon la structure des têtes d'attention.
limites.complexite_implementation: L'intégration de LowRAM nécessite des modifications fines du pipeline d'inférence, notamment pour la gestion dynamique des résidus et la reconstruction sélective, ce qui peut compliquer son adoption dans des frameworks existants.

deep_analysis.verdict: LowRAM représente une avancée significative pour la compression du cache KV, combinant efficacité et composabilité, mais son adoption dépendra de la tolérance aux surcharges en préremplissage et de la facilité d'intégration dans les infrastructures existantes.

items.title: AutoCompress: Automated Hardware-Guided Model Compression
items.summary: LLM pruning must preserve quality while meeting hardware- and workload-specific constraints on latency, throughput, and memory. Existing pruning workflows often target parameter counts, requiring practitioners to manually select model sizes that meet latency, throughput, and GPU memory limits. However, parameter count alone does not predict these metrics, which depend on the model architecture, workload, hardware, and serving engine. We introduce AutoCompress, a hardware-guided compression framework that directly incorporates such constraints into differentiable architecture search. AutoCompress jointly optimizes global and per-layer structure to produce heterogeneous architectures, guided by serving-engine cost models validated against end-to-end latency, throughput, and memory measurements. We evaluate AutoCompress on long-context local coding, batched datacenter serving, and latency-sensitive in-game interaction. Compared to the state-of-the-art Minitron pruning framework, AutoCompress improves average accuracy across eight benchmarks by 6.57, 2.35, and 0.57 percentage points on RTX 5070, RTX 5080, and H100, respectively. AutoCompress also compresses Nemotron 3.5 Super from 120B to 74B parameters for single-B200 BF16 serving at 128K context, retaining 95% of its mean benchmark score.
items.tldr: AutoCompress propose un cadre de pruning guidé par le matériel pour optimiser les architectures des LLM en intégrant directement les contraintes de latence, débit et mémoire. Il améliore significativement la précision par rapport aux méthodes existantes (ex. Minitron) tout en respectant les contraintes hardware spécifiques (RTX 5070, H100).

deep_analysis.probleme: La compression de modèles d'IA (pruning) vise à réduire leur taille tout en préservant leur qualité, mais elle doit aussi respecter des contraintes matérielles et opérationnelles spécifiques, comme la latence, le débit et la mémoire GPU. Actuellement, les méthodes de pruning se concentrent souvent sur le nombre de paramètres, sans garantir que ces contraintes seront satisfaites, car ces métriques dépendent de l'architecture du modèle, du workload, du matériel et du moteur d'inférence utilisé.
deep_analysis.methode: AutoCompress est un framework de compression guidé par le matériel qui intègre directement ces contraintes dans une recherche d'architecture différentiable. Il optimise conjointement la structure globale et par couche du modèle pour produire des architectures hétérogènes, en s'appuyant sur des modèles de coût validés par des mesures réelles de latence, débit et mémoire. Cette approche utilise des modèles de coût spécifiques aux moteurs d'inférence pour guider la compression, évitant ainsi les approximations basées uniquement sur le nombre de paramètres. Le framework prend en compte des scénarios variés, comme le traitement de longs contextes ou des interactions en temps réel.
deep_analysis.resultats: AutoCompress surpasse le framework de pruning Minitron sur plusieurs benchmarks, avec des gains moyens de précision de 6,57 points de pourcentage sur RTX 5070, 2,35 sur RTX 5080 et 0,57 sur H100. Il permet également de compresser le modèle Nemotron 3.5 Super de 120 milliards à 74 milliards de paramètres pour une inférence en BF16 sur un seul GPU B200 avec un contexte de 128K, tout en conservant 95 % de sa performance moyenne sur les benchmarks.
deep_analysis.limites: Les détails techniques sur la manière dont les modèles de coût sont construits et validés restent flous, ce qui peut soulever des questions sur leur généralisabilité à d'autres architectures ou matériels. De plus, l'évaluation se limite à des benchmarks spécifiques et à des scénarios d'utilisation prédéfinis, sans garantie que les performances se maintiendront dans des contextes plus variés ou imprévus.
deep_analysis.verdict: AutoCompress mérite une attention particulière pour son approche innovante d'intégration des contraintes matérielles dans la compression de modèles, offrant des gains tangibles en précision et en efficacité, mais son applicabilité à large échelle reste à démontrer.

items.title: Authorization Drift in LLM Agents: Evaluating Boundary Compliance in Multi-Step Tool Use
items.summary: LLM agents can exceed their authorization boundaries while pursuing user goals without an adversary. We formalize this phenomenon as authorization drift across data, tool, scope, and time, and introduce the Authorization Drift Benchmark (ADB): 648 samples across seven domains, each pairing a sufficient compliant path with an attractive unauthorized shortcut. To ensure executable tasks, tempting shortcuts, and feasible compliant paths, Staged Execution-Reflective Synthesis (SERS) grounds benchmark validation in real agent rollouts rather than LLM self-critique. Across 13 LLMs and three frameworks (25,207 trajectories), greater capability accompanies greater drift, with frontier-capable models exhibiting drift rates of 0.43 to 0.61. Yet 86.18% of tasks admit an observed clean-success trajectory, showing that drift is avoidable. Drift is persistent and dominated by early data over-collection; apparent improvements under agentic scaffolds coincide with collapsing clean-completion performance. To understand potential harms to individuals and society, we map drift points to legal provisions across four jurisdictions, connecting overreach to privacy and information-security concerns. Data minimisation is the most frequently implicated provision, and 93.5% of legally grounded drifting runs map to multiple jurisdictions, making the potential consequences of authorization drift more interpretable.
items.tldr: ADB formalise le 'drift d'autorisation' dans les agents LLM (dépassement involontaire des limites) et propose un benchmark de 648 tâches avec des chemins conformes vs. raccourcis tentants. Les modèles frontaliers montrent un taux de drift de 43-61%, mais 86% des tâches admettent une solution conforme, soulignant des marges d'amélioration.

deep_analysis.probleme: Cette publication aborde le phénomène de *dérive d'autorisation* dans les agents basés sur les LLM (Large Language Models), où ces derniers dépassent leurs limites d'autorisation initiales lors de l'exécution de tâches multi-étapes pour atteindre un objectif utilisateur, sans intervention malveillante. Le problème vise à formaliser et évaluer ce risque, notamment en matière de conformité aux frontières d'accès aux données, aux outils, au périmètre d'action et au temps, afin de prévenir des atteintes potentielles à la vie privée ou à la sécurité de l'information.

methode.formalisation: Les auteurs définissent la *dérive d'autorisation* selon quatre dimensions : données (accès non autorisé), outils (utilisation détournée), scope (dépassement du périmètre fonctionnel) et temps (persistance des accès).
methode.benchmark: Ils introduisent l'*Authorization Drift Benchmark (ADB)*, composé de 648 échantillons répartis sur sept domaines, chacun proposant un chemin conforme suffisant et une *tentation* (shortcut non autorisé mais attractif).
methode.validation: Pour garantir des tâches exécutables, des raccourcis tentants et des chemins conformes réalistes, la méthode *Staged Execution-Reflective Synthesis (SERS)* ancre la validation dans des exécutions réelles d'agents plutôt que dans une auto-critique par LLM.
methode.evaluation: 13 modèles de LLM et 3 frameworks ont été testés (25 207 trajectoires), avec une analyse des taux de dérive et des performances de conformité. Une cartographie des points de dérive a été réalisée vers des dispositions légales de quatre juridictions pour évaluer les risques concrets.

resultats.taux_de_derive: Les modèles les plus performants (*frontier-capable*) affichent des taux de dérive élevés, compris entre 0,43 et 0,61, démontrant que l'augmentation des capacités s'accompagne d'un risque accru de dépassement d'autorisation.
resultats.viabilite_conforme: 86,18 % des tâches admettent au moins une trajectoire conforme réussie (*clean-success*), prouvant que la dérive n'est pas inévitable mais dépend des choix de conception.
resultats.persistance: La dérive est persistante et dominée par une *sur-collecte précoce de données*, tandis que les améliorations apparentes sous des *scaffolds agentiques* coïncident avec une chute des performances de conformité.
resultats.implications_legales: 93,5 % des exécutions non conformes mais *légalement ancrées* concernent plusieurs juridictions, avec un focus sur le *principe de minimisation des données* (protection de la vie privée).

limites.representativite: Le benchmark ADB, bien que diversifié, repose sur des scénarios synthétiques. Son adéquation avec des cas réels complexes ou des environnements dynamiques reste à démontrer.
limites.biais_methodologique: La validation par SERS dépend de la qualité des *rollouts* d'agents, qui pourraient introduire des biais liés aux frameworks ou aux modèles testés, limitant la généralisabilité.
limites.interpretation_legale: La cartographie juridique est théorique et ne reflète pas nécessairement l'application concrète des lois, notamment en l'absence de jurisprudence sur les LLM.

deep_analysis.verdict: Ce travail mérite une attention particulière pour son approche systématique du risque de dérive d'autorisation dans les LLM, offrant des outils concrets pour évaluer et atténuer un enjeu critique de sécurité et de conformité, malgré des limites inhérentes à sa méthodologie expérimentale.

items.title: AgentBaton: Efficient Model Collaboration in Agentic Tasks
items.summary: Solving long-horizon agentic tasks requires language agents to interact with their environments over multiple steps, and reliable performance often comes from the expensive capable models available through cloud providers. Meanwhile, alternative efficient models with inferior performance but a much lower cost are emerging, including lower-tier cloud models and smaller open-weights models deployable on local hardware. This raises a natural question that remains less explored than traditional query-level routing: can capable and efficient models collaborate within a single long-horizon agentic task to substantially reduce cost while preserving task accuracy? In this paper, we systematically investigate key design choices for such collaboration through model handoffs, where one model takes over from another, focusing on handoff direction and context transfer. We find that efficient-to-capable handoffs generally underperform capable-only execution with limited or even no cost reduction, whereas capable-to-efficient handoffs at suitable stages of task progress largely preserve or even improve accuracy while substantially reducing cost. These findings suggest that a one-time, simple, well-timed handoff strategy is good enough for cost-effective agent collaboration, motivating AgentBaton, a lightweight detector that learns when to hand off from recurring patterns in task progress. Across 11 model pairs and two representative benchmarks, AgentBaton reduces API costs by 65.9% on average while largely preserving task accuracy, with accuracy gains of up to 8.8 percentage points over capable-only execution. Experiments across various reasoning-effort settings further show that AgentBaton extends the empirical accuracy-cost Pareto frontier.
items.tldr: AgentBaton explore la collaboration efficace entre modèles (capables vs. légers) dans des tâches agentiques longues, démontrant que des handoffs capables vers efficaces réduisent les coûts tout en préservant la performance.

items.title: The Last Mile to the Real World: Agent-Native Primitives as Reusable Building Blocks for Solving Real-World Tasks
items.summary: How can an agent handle a real-world task end to end? Frontier models with their own harnesses still fall short on real-world benchmarks: on Terminal-Bench 4.0, GPT-5.6 Sol with Codex resolves 37.3% of the tasks and Claude Opus 5 with Claude Code 51.8%. These tasks fail at the step from reaching a resource to applying it, which we call the last mile to the real world. Existing approaches put the resource within reach but leave the competence to apply it with the caller, so each harness rebuilds that competence. We introduce agent-native primitives, reusable units that equip a resource with a resident LLM that applies it in context and communicates with other primitives, and HEELO (Harness Engineering around Evolving Agent-Native Primitives for the Last Mile to Real-WOrld Tasks), a harness engineering framework that builds each task's harness from a library of such primitives. HEELO composes the primitives a task needs into a task-specific graph, verifies the result against evidence from the environment, revises the primitives a failure implicates, and admits new or improved primitives after validation. We instantiate HEELO with eight primitive families, each built for one kind of task, and evaluate them on more than twenty benchmarks. Dev-Primitives raise Terminal-Bench 4.0 resolution from 37.3% under Codex to 55.5% on the same backbone, Harness Primitives composed per task raise Terminal-Bench 2.0 Pass@1 from 60.0% for the seed harness to 72.2%, Tool Primitives raise ToolBench pass rate from 55.8% to 75.1%, and Navigation Primitives raise GAIA-Text-103 accuracy from 45.6% to 58.3%. On the 46 real-world tasks of our heelo.dev platform, Claude Opus 5.5 with Claude Code and GPT-6.1 Sol with Codex complete 9 each on their own and 39 and 35 when connected to HEELO through our MCP server, with 1.9times and 2.3times less time and 1.55times lower cost per completed task.
items.tldr: HEELO introduit des 'primitives natives pour agents' comme blocs modulaires pour résoudre des tâches réelles, réduisant l'écart entre la résolution de ressources et leur application concrète dans des environnements complexes.

items.title: Hierarchical Residuals: A Minimalist Decoupling of Residual Width from Compute Width
items.summary: Residual connections underpin Transformers, but they implicitly tie the residual width carried through depth to the compute width used inside each layer. We introduce Hierarchical Residuals (HiRes), a minimalist architectural change that decouples these dimensions, widening the residual state while keeping per-layer compute width fixed. HiRes groups layers into blocks: standard d-dimensional PreNorm layers operate inside each block, while a wider D-dimensional PostNorm outer residual connects blocks. Learned read/write projections bridge the two spaces at block boundaries, leaving individual Transformer layers unchanged. Across different model sizes and depths, HiRes consistently outperforms vanilla residual addition, with fitted scaling laws indicating a 1.30-fold improvement in FLOPs efficiency. On OLMoE-1B-7B pretraining for 500B tokens, HiRes achieves 0.0208 lower training loss and 1.14-point higher downstream accuracy. HiRes is also competitive with other residual expansion methods such as VWN, mHC and AttnRes with less activation memory and I/O costs. Built from only dense projections and normalizations, it requires neither specialized kernels nor infrastructure-level optimizations. HiRes thus exposes residual width as a practical scaling variable using only standard operators.
items.tldr: HiRes decouple la largeur résiduelle de la largeur de calcul dans les Transformers via des blocs hiérarchiques, améliorant l'efficacité FLOPs de 1.30x. Sur OLMoE-1B-7B, HiRes réduit la perte d'entraînement et améliore la précision en aval avec moins de mémoire d'activation.

items.title: EvoWorld: Towards Out-of-Sight World Evolution in Generative Video Models
items.summary: Generative video models are increasingly used as visual world simulators, yet their primary strength lies in rendering plausible pixels rather than reasoning about how a world should evolve. Coherent world evolution requires more than visual fidelity: when an event occurs, a model must infer its consequences for the entities in the world and then render the resulting state. For example, after a wild beast appears, the model should not only depict the wild beast, but also infer whether a nearby person should flee, take cover, or fight back based on the realized scene. Existing diffusion-based video models lack an explicit mechanism for maintaining world state and reasoning over such event-conditioned consequences, often producing visually plausible but behaviorally static or causally inconsistent outputs. To make this reasoning gap concrete and measurable, we propose a new problem, Out-of-Sight Causal Evolution, which requires a model to render an event, reason about its consequences for the evolving world state, and reveal a causally plausible outcome as the world continues to evolve, even out of sight. As a baseline reference solution, we introduce EvoWorld, a brain-renderer collaboration framework in which a vision-language model serves as the world brain: it observes generated segments, maintains an evolving account of the world, and reasons about plausible state transitions, while a segment-autoregressive video renderer realizes them visually. We further introduce EvoWorld-Data and EvoWorld-Bench for training and evaluating event realization, causal reactions, and revisit consistency. Experiments show that EvoWorld substantially improves event-conditioned causal evolution over recent models while preserving visual quality and consistency, establishing a reference point for reasoning-guided, autonomous world evolution beyond the current field of view.
items.tldr: EvoWorld aborde le problème de l'évolution causale des mondes simulés par IA, proposant un nouveau benchmark (Out-of-Sight Causal Evolution) et un modèle de type 'brain-renderer' pour raisonner sur les conséquences d'événements hors-champ.

items.title: Steerable Multi-Objective Group-Relative Preference Optimization with Jointly Trained Low-Rank Adapters
items.summary: Language model deployment often requires different trade-offs between competing objectives as user preferences change, yet standard post-training methods typically produce a single policy for a fixed objective weighting. We introduce LambdaMix, a new parameter efficient method for learning a preference conditioned family of policies with group-relative online reinforcement learning. LambdaMix jointly trains one low-rank adapter per objective over a frozen base model. One preference vector selects the adapter mixture that generates responses and weights the separately normalized rewards used to update the adapters. A single training run supports changing preferences at inference without further optimization. We experiment with four models on helpfulness and harmlessness and on solving math problems while following instructions. We also evaluate the two largest models on rewriting comments to preserve wording while reducing clues about personal attributes. On the first two tasks, LambdaMix achieves higher hypervolume than all evaluated conditioned and policy merging baselines across all four models. LambdaMix uses fewer training completions and stores fewer adapter parameters than a set of GRPO specialist policies. With architecture and initialization fixed, varying adapter mixtures and objective weights together gives wider score ranges and higher coverage than varying either alone.
items.tldr: LambdaMix introduit une méthode d'optimisation multi-objectifs pour les LLM, permettant d'adapter dynamiquement les préférences utilisateur via des adapters à rang faible entraînés conjointement. Les résultats montrent une meilleure hypervolume que les baselines existantes, avec un coût de stockage et d'entraînement réduit.

items.title: Where to Connect? Boosting MLLMs via Dynamic Gated Pathways across ALL ViT and LLM Layers
items.summary: A central yet under-explored question in Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) is where to connect---how visual information from a hierarchical vision encoder should be wired into the layer-wise semantics of a large language model. Mainstream MLLMs inject a fixed single-layer visual representation into the LLM and treat all LLM layers as a single consumer, ignoring that different layers demand different visual granularities. Recent multi-layer fusion methods either compress hierarchical features on the encoder side or rely on predefined sparse or hierarchical layer-to-layer connections, and therefore stop short of modeling adaptive cross-layer interactions between the ViT and LLM hierarchies. We address this gap with DGP (Dynamic Gated Pathways), a routing mechanism that establishes all-to-all connections between every ViT layer and every LLM layer, with each LLM layer dynamically gating its preference over visual layers conditioned on its own semantic state. Built on top of LLaVA-1.5-7B and 13B, DGP delivers consistent gains over the LLaVA-1.5-7B baseline (e.g., +4.2 on SQA^{I}, +3.3 on MM-Vet, +3.1 on VizWiz and LLaVA^{W}) and surpasses prior multi-layer visual fusion methods on most benchmarks. Layer-wise routing analyses further show that different LLM layers do select different visual granularities on demand, supporting both the effectiveness and interpretability of the proposed dynamic gated pathways. The code is available: https://github.com/YingyingYan1/DGP.
items.tldr: DGP propose un mécanisme de routage dynamique pour connecter toutes les couches d'un ViT à toutes celles d'un LLM dans les MLLMs, adaptant la granularité visuelle aux besoins sémantiques des couches du LLM. Sur LLaVA-1.5, DGP améliore les performances (ex: +4.2 sur SQA^I) par rapport aux méthodes existantes.

items.title: LongBanana: An Expert-Verified Benchmark for Long-Context Multi-Reference Image Synthesis
items.summary: We introduce LongBanana, to our knowledge the first expert-designed and expert-verified benchmark for long-context multi-reference image synthesis in the age of agent-driven image generation. The task requires retrieving dispersed visual evidence, rejecting distractors, binding entities and relations, and composing one coherent final image from multiple references. LongBanana contains 90 carefully designed tasks organized by a 3-by-3 taxonomy; each task includes about 32 reference images, 20 constraints, and 50 evaluation items, yielding 4,670 expert-specified atomic evaluation items in total. Its graph-grounded evaluation design instantiates each task with reference images and an entity-relation graph, then converts node, edge, and whole-graph obligations into checklist items for Content Fidelity, Relational Binding, and Global Constraint Satisfaction. Reviewed expert labels include a 15% double-labeled subset with 89.4% exact agreement and 0.83 quadratic weighted kappa. We further introduce LongBanana-Gen, an agent-harness framework for long-horizon image generation; experiments show that minimal agent harnesses improve over direct generation, while a ReAct-Plan-Exec-Reflect (RPR) workflow yields harness-dependent gains by strengthening evidence grounding and repair. Together, LongBanana provides an auditable testbed for measuring dense visual evidence use and a shared target for developing stronger agent-driven image-generation systems. Code and data are available at the project page: https://long-banana.com/.
items.tldr: LongBanana introduit un benchmark expert-validé pour l'évaluation de la synthèse d'images multi-références en contexte long, combinant des tâches complexes (fidélité contextuelle, binding relationnel) et un cadre d'évaluation graphique. Il démontre l'avantage des agents (ex. RPR) sur les approches directes.

items.title: P^2-MOPD: Accelerating Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation via Parameter Priors
items.summary: Multi-teacher on-policy distillation consolidates expert capabilities by supervising student-generated trajectories, whereas task arithmetic offers a training-free alternative through linear parameter combinations. We view the linear combination of student and expert parameters as a single differentiable model and propose P^2-MOPD, which jointly optimizes the mixing coefficients and the student weights under the same on-policy distillation objective. Unlike task arithmetic, which stays within the span of the frozen student and expert parameters for any choice of merging coefficients, P^2-MOPD keeps the student trainable, so the experts act as parameter priors without confining it to this span. Across four domains at 1.7B and 4B scales, P^2-MOPD achieves faster and more balanced recovery than MOPD from the same initialization, surpassing its final average recovery in half the training steps. At the end of training, our 1.7B model reaches 94.7% average recovery, versus 80.9% for MOPD.
items.tldr: P²-MOPD accélère la distillation multi-enseignants en optimisant conjointement les coefficients de mélange et les poids du modèle étudiant, atteignant 94.7% de récupération moyenne (vs 80.9% pour MOPD) en moitié moins d'étapes, grâce à une approche basée sur des *parameter priors*.

items.title: Fast and Exact Relative-Position Attention via Structure-Aware Kernels
items.summary: Relative-position attention mechanisms offer compelling alternatives to RoPE across various transformer architectures, delivering superior performance in domains such as audio. These mechanisms typically modify attention scores by adding content-position or bias-position terms. Unlike RoPE, which encodes position via per-token rotations directly on the queries and keys, relative-position terms generally require pairwise offset-dependent computation or lookups, complicating their integration into fused attention kernels and introducing severe memory, bandwidth, and compute overheads as sequences scale. To address this bottleneck, we propose an exact attention algorithm that incorporates additive relative-position terms into FlashAttention-style tiled computation. Our method (1) uses offset-aware tiling to avoid redundant indexing and memory accesses, (2) computes only the necessary key/query-relation products and reuses them across token pairs in both forward and backward passes, and (3) uses offset-based gradient sharding and aggregation, eliminating atomic contention. We provide a unified, efficient Triton implementation across diverse relative-position attention mechanisms and evaluate it against naive and specialized implementations. For 8K-token sequences, our method speeds up the forward (backward) pass by 1.8-6.4times (2.0-21times) and reduces peak memory up to 2.9-128times (1.4-54times) over the strongest baseline for each mechanism, enabling long-context end-to-end transcription that is 1.8times faster and uses 2.4times less memory. Our method thus provides a drop-in, hardware-efficient solution for scaling relative-position attention transformers.
items.tldr: Ce papier propose un algorithme exact pour l'attention relative-position (alternative à RoPE) via des noyaux structure-aware, optimisé pour FlashAttention. Il réduit les overheads mémoire/calcul et permet une intégration efficace dans les kernels fusionnés, avec une implémentation Triton unifiée.

items.title: Video-Coder: Reinforcing Agentic Coding for Video Generation
items.summary: Recent years have witnessed remarkable progress in video generation in terms of visual quality and temporal consistency. However, generating videos with precise spatial structure, coherent motion dynamics, and controllable scene composition remains challenging. In this paper, we introduce Video-Coder, the first attempt to train a code-driven video generation agent, which autonomously writes and executes code to construct a dynamic 3D scene (Draft Video) that provides structure and motion signals to downstream video generators. To support this paradigm, we design a dedicated data pipeline and curate two high-quality datasets, Video-Coder-SFT-6k and Video-Coder-RL-2k, which contain diverse prompts and ground-truth reference videos. We further develop the Video- Coder Harness, a unified interactive environment integrating code execution, 3D scene rendering, and execution feedback for agent training and inference. We then train Video-Coder with SFT fol- lowed by harness-native agentic reinforcement learning with dual reward feedback, which combines execution-based and video-based rewards. Additionally, we design an annealing training strategy that gradually reduces the execution reward over time, allowing the model to rely more on the video reward in the later training stages. Experiments show that Video-Coder achieves significant gains, improving Minimax-H3 by approximately 7 points on PhyGenBench and 24 points on VBench-2.0. We hope this work can serve as an open foundation for coding agents in video generation, and we fully open-source our data, models, and code
items.tldr: Video-Coder introduit un agent de génération vidéo basé sur le code pour construire des scènes 3D dynamiques, combinant apprentissage par renforcement et données structurées pour améliorer la cohérence spatiale et temporelle des vidéos générées.

items.title: Beneath the Surface: What We Overlook When We Talk About Agent Evolution
items.summary: Agent harness evolution enables recursive self-improvement (RSI) without updating model weights. We examine whether higher benchmark scores yield reliable, efficient, and transferable improvement. We evaluate four methods across harnesses, general and coding tasks. Repeated evaluations, controlled agent expansion, component interventions, and admission replays reveal recurring patterns. All sixteen evolved agents gain previously uncovered tasks while losing previously covered ones. In one general-task case, reliability rises by 5.2 points despite losing ten previously covered tasks. Most reliability gains also increase deployment cost. Specific changes usually outperform generic reminders, but their benefits can change when combined. The highest-scoring agent does not yield the largest mean improvement in any of our four pools, and stricter admission can discard useful alternatives. Transfer selectively preserves gains: coverage usually falls on the general-task target across both harness types and paradigms, but rises on the coding target with the outer-layer-only harness. These findings motivate preservation-aware evaluation, tested decision rules, and explicit applicability conditions. As a constructive follow-up, EvoAudit turns these diagnostics into revisions of select, analyze, mutate, and gate, achieving the best performance.
items.tldr: L'étude 'Beneath the Surface' analyse l'évolution des agents via des harnais, révélant que les gains de performance s'accompagnent souvent de pertes de couverture et de coûts accrus, soulignant la nécessité d'évaluations préservatrices.

items.title: Knowing When to Teach: Learning from Teachable Prefixes in Multilingual Reasoning Distillation
items.summary: On-Policy Self-Distillation (OPSD) improves reasoning by training a student on its own reasoning, using the same model conditioned on reference solutions as a teacher. Applying OPSD to multilingual reasoning requires the teacher to provide useful feedback across languages, even when the student makes mistakes in intermediate steps. We observe a phenomenon we call Teacher Drift: as these mistakes accumulate, the teacher may follow the student's incorrect steps instead of correcting them. Our analysis shows that this shift tends to occur earlier in lower-resource languages. To account for these differences across languages, we propose Teachable On-Policy Self-Distillation (TOPSD), which determines where and whether teacher supervision should be applied to each reasoning trajectory. TOPSD uses teacher-student likelihood to estimate where drift begins and select a prefix for supervision. It then verifies whether the teacher can recover the correct answer from that prefix, applying distillation only to prefixes that pass verification. Experiments on multilingual mathematical reasoning across ten languages and three model scales show that TOPSD consistently outperforms conventional OPSD, particularly in low- and medium-resource languages.
items.tldr: TOPSD améliore la distillation auto-supervisée multilingue en détectant et corrigeant le 'Teacher Drift' (dérive du professeur) via des préfixes enseignables. Les expériences sur 10 langues et 3 échelles de modèles montrent des gains systématiques par rapport à l'OPSD classique.

items.title: LLMs Don't Know What They Know: Benchmarking Temporal Self-Knowledge for Financial Backtesting
items.summary: Financial backtests of large language models (LLMs) are meaningful only if the model did not already know the outcomes it is asked to predict. Practitioners guard against this by trusting a vendor's stated knowledge cutoff, by asking the model what it knows, or by instructing it to answer as of a past date. To verify whether any of these safeguards can be trusted, we introduce FinDendro, a benchmark of 2,226 dated U.S. facts from 1999 to 2026, covering monthly macroeconomic series, month-end stock prices and Federal Reserve decisions. Each fact yields four prompts: a value question, Recall and Predict questions that pair each candidate value with a claim of knowing or guessing without a declared date, and a Predict question with a historical declared date. Controls for persistence and dominant outcomes keep chance accuracy near 0.27. Results show that for most frontier models, self-reports understate knowledge. GPT-5 answers 76% of controlled facts correctly but claims to know 38%, and answers 61% of the facts it says it does not know. Knowledge claims can persist beyond the measured knowledge boundary, by up to seven quarters, and a declared date removes most of the claims of prior knowledge while leaving accuracy unchanged. Backtests inside a model's training window therefore cannot be certified leak-free by self-report, instruction or stated cutoff. These findings motivate behavioral measurement of temporal knowledge boundaries, and FinDendro provides a benchmark and procedure for selecting backtest periods based on demonstrated factual knowledge.
items.tldr: FinDendro évalue la *self-knowledge* temporelle des LLM en finance, révélant que les modèles surestiment leur connaissance des données (ex. GPT-5 répond correctement à 76% des faits mais n'en revendique que 38%), avec des biais persistants au-delà des cutoffs déclarés.

items.title: Frontier3DBench: Benchmarking Coding Agents for 3D Creation across Objects, Scenes, and Interactive Open Worlds
items.summary: Coding agents combine visual understanding with program execution, offering a new route to automated 3D creation. By translating images and instructions into editable programs, they bring reconstruction, generation, and editing into a shared workflow. Yet existing benchmarks fragment evaluation across task scopes and protocols, leaving their capabilities across construction levels unclear. We propose Frontier3DBench, a unified benchmark of 145 tasks across 9 categories spanning object, scene, and interactive open-world creation, with joint evaluation of appearance, structure, and behavior. Experiments with 11 model-harness configurations reveal strengths that vary by level: GPT-6.1-sol leads the object and scene levels and achieves the highest overall score of 66.02/100, whereas GPT-6-astra leads interactive world construction. However, all configurations score lower on reference reconstruction than on text-driven generation in object and scene tasks. Producing plausible content thus remains easier than reproducing specified geometry, layouts, and visual details. Moreover, generated worlds average 83.08/100 on local mechanisms but only 20.82 on motion clearance and 30.26 on stateful workflows: individual mechanisms often function, whereas complete activities that require coordinated actions and persistent state remain difficult. These results identify reference fidelity and coordinated activity completion as central bottlenecks for coding agents in 3D creation.
items.tldr: Frontier3DBench évalue les *coding agents* pour la création 3D (objets, scènes, mondes interactifs) sur 145 tâches, montrant que les modèles (ex. GPT-6.1-sol) excellent en génération mais échouent sur la reconstruction fidèle de géométries complexes.

items.title: Exploring Weight-Space Programming: Capabilities, Generalization, and Limitations
items.summary: Weight-Space Programming (WSP) enables reasoning agents to directly inspect and modify neural network parameters, offering an alternative to gradient-based model adaptation. However, its capabilities, cross-task generalization, and practical limitations remain insufficiently understood. We systematically investigate WSP through 16 editing trajectories across seven benchmarks and two model scales (Qwen3.5-0.8B and Qwen3.5-9B). Our findings reveal three key insights. First, WSP can achieve substantial performance gains through highly localized interventions. On full held-out evaluations, accuracy improves by up to 29.45, 4.42, 36.72, and 17.11 percentage points on MATH-500, GPQA Diamond, IFEval, and SciBench, respectively. Notably, modifying only 1,023 parameters yields a 29.45-point improvement. Second, WSP exhibits promising but uneven cross-task generalization. A Math-edited checkpoint improves GPQA Diamond, IFEval, and SciBench by 3.03, 12.18, and 20.10 points, respectively, without further editing, while leaving SciCode performance unchanged. Third, effective editing remains challenging and inconsistent. Outcomes vary substantially across trajectories, and six of the 16 trajectories retain the original weights when candidate improvements cannot be reliably validated. Together, these results highlight WSP's potential for highly localized model adaptation while revealing important challenges in intervention discovery, reliability, and cross-task transfer. Homepage: https://wsp-scope.github.io/ GitHub: https://github.com/WSP-Scope/WSP-Scope-Project
items.tldr: Weight-Space Programming (WSP) permet de modifier directement les paramètres d'un modèle pour améliorer ses performances, avec des gains significatifs (jusqu'à +29.45 points) en modifiant seulement 1 023 paramètres, mais avec une généralisation inégale.

items.title: Human-Centred, Risk-Constrained Evaluation of Financial Document Recognition: Evidence, Critical Errors, and Selective Automation
items.summary: Financial document recognition is often assessed using character and word error rates, although these metrics do not express whether a system preserves the financial facts on which people and organisations act. This paper develops a human-centred, risk-constrained framework for evaluating financial document recognition as evidence recovery and decision support. It defines typed financial facts linked to visible source regions and separates verbatim transcription, deterministic normalization, and business interpretation. A layered quality model covers text, localization, layout, tables, fields, fact correctness, evidence grounding, uncertainty, robustness, and operational performance. Non-compensatory acceptance gates use one-sided uncertainty bounds for critical-field errors, preventing strong aggregate scores from masking failures in amounts, identifiers, signs, periods, or entity associations. Selective automation is formulated as a constrained routing problem that accounts for residual risk, human-review capacity, and review cost. The framework further specifies annotation and adjudication procedures, leakage-resistant benchmark partitions, statistical estimands, subgroup analyses, and a reproducibility card. Formal results establish the limitations of compensatory scoring, the non-zero upper risk bound after zero observed errors, and a loss sensitive decision rule for routing uncertain cases to human review. The contribution is theoretical and methodological; no new model, dataset, or empirical performance result is claimed.
items.tldr: Ce travail propose un cadre d'évaluation centré sur l'humain pour la reconnaissance de documents financiers, intégrant des contraintes de risque et des erreurs critiques (montants, identifiants). Il formalise la séparation entre transcription, normalisation et interprétation métier, avec des gates d'acceptation non compensatoires.

items.title: SplatAnything: Gaussian Spacing Normalization for Feed-forward 3DGS across Arbitrary Scenes
items.summary: We identify a key limitation of existing feed-forward 3DGS methods: Gaussian attributes are typically predicted in a radial-distance-normalized space that canonicalizes a global radial statistic of the reconstructed geometry, while the spacing between neighboring Gaussian centers can still vary substantially across scene scales and camera configurations. This mismatch induces systematic shifts in Gaussian-scale targets, leading to ambiguous supervision. To address this, we propose SplatAnything with Gaussian Spacing Normalization (GSNorm), which canonicalizes a robust scene-level statistic of Gaussian spacing to provide a more consistent spatial reference for Gaussian prediction. To rigorously assess our method, we further establish a systematic benchmark spanning diverse datasets, input sparsity levels, and challenging extrapolated viewpoints. Extensive experiments demonstrate that SplatAnything achieves state-of-the-art performance, with particularly strong gains under substantial variations in scene scale and viewpoint.
items.tldr: SplatAnything introduit GSNorm pour normaliser l'espacement des Gaussiens dans les méthodes 3DGS feed-forward, améliorant les performances (notamment pour les scènes à grande variabilité d'échelle) via une supervision plus cohérente des attributs géométriques.

items.title: OmniLatent: Unified Latent for 3D Part Modeling
items.summary: 3D part decomposition is a central capability for editable asset creation, yet existing workflows typically segment a completed mesh as a post-processing step, making the result sensitive to geometric artifacts, texture ambiguity, and limited part-level annotations. We present OmniLatent, a unified latent modeling framework for 3D part decomposition. Instead of predicting part labels in isolation, OmniLatent learns a shared latent space that jointly encodes geometry, deformation, appearance, and binary part IDs, allowing data-rich geometric and visual priors to support data-scarce part learning. Given a single input image, the base model generates geometry, deformation, texture, and surface part IDs in one pass, producing a part-aware 3D asset without a separate segmentation stage. We further tune the pretrained model for two extensions: a point-prompt adapter that maps arbitrary 3D point prompts with binary part IDs into latent tokens for full segmentation, refinement, and part subdivision, and an amodal part completion model that completes partial surface masks into a coherent full-object decomposition through dynamic per-part token allocation, cross-attention to the given geometry latent, and alternating part-local and global attention. Extensive experiments show that OmniLatent produces semantically meaningful part segmentations with precise boundaries, supports interactive part editing, and completes partial part observations while preserving global object consistency.
items.tldr: OmniLatent propose un cadre latent unifié pour la décomposition 3D en parties, intégrant géométrie, texture et segmentation en un seul passage à partir d'une image 2D, réduisant les artefacts et améliorant l'efficacité par rapport aux méthodes post-processing.

items.title: OneTrans-GSR: A Generative Slate Ranking Paradigm Unifying Reranking and Mix-Ranking with One Autoregressive Transformer
items.summary: Industrial recommender systems allocate substantial computation to pointwise candidate scoring, yet separate reranking and mix-ranking stages still assemble the final exposure slate using hand-crafted rules and specialized low-capacity models. Mix-ranking combines product cards, short videos, livestreams, and advertising cards supplied by distinct upstream business channels. Although these rules and models encode valuable domain knowledge, they are inherently limited in leveraging additional data and computation. They constrain the combinatorial space of candidate slates and determine objective trade-offs through manual tuning. To enable scalable and effective slate generation, we reformulate reranking and mix-ranking as a unified learning problem whose performance can improve with computation. Specifically, we instantiate this formulation across the reranking and mix-ranking stages and propose OneTrans-GSR, a single decoder-only policy that extends our deployed OneTrans backbone to generate the exposure slate end-to-end. During training, a reward model evaluates complete slates and guides reinforcement learning toward slate-level and long-term objectives. During decoding, business constraints are explicitly enforced. Offline evaluation shows that slate quality consistently improves as reward-model and policy compute increase. Deployed in a large-scale industrial recommendation system, OneTrans-GSR mixes heterogeneous content types within a unified slate. In online A/B tests, it improves GMV/u by 2.63%, advertiser value by 2.06%, and repurchase rate by 2.03%, while reducing end-to-end latency across the reranking and mix-ranking stages by 13%. These results mark a paradigm shift in slate generation: moving beyond human-engineered heuristics toward a general learned policy creates a scalable path for further algorithmic optimization and compute-driven improvement.
items.tldr: OneTrans-GSR unifie le reranking et le mix-ranking en un seul modèle autoregressif pour les systèmes de recommandation, optimisant les slates de manière end-to-end via RL guidé par un reward model, tout en conservant l'interprétabilité des règles métiers.

items.title: Confucius4-R2T2: A Stable-Prefix Streaming ASR Model for Real Real-Time Transcription
items.summary: Streaming speech recognition is increasingly consumed by machines, such as translators and voice agents, that act on each token as it appears. A token that is later revised costs wasted work or a wrong action. In this work, we present Confucius4-R2T2 (short for Real Real-Time Transcription), a stable-prefix streaming ASR model that never modifies its earlier output while maintaining high accuracy and low latency. R2T2 is obtained by post-training Qwen3-ASR-1.7B on 1,500 hours of Chinese and English audio while freezing its pre-trained audio encoder and projector. The adaptation is based on the concept of Longest Stable Prefix (LSP), a new notion that we introduce in this work. We prove that LSP is monotone under the prefix order, consistent with the full-audio output, and maximal among labels that equal a whole earlier output. Learning from LSP labels converts a full-context model into a stable-prefix streaming one without any architectural change. Extensive evaluations show that R2T2 brings streaming recognition close to the base model's full-context quality while delivering stable text with low emission lag. Its gains extend beyond the post-training languages, demonstrating a practical path from full-context ASR to stable streaming. We open-source the model weights and code at https://huggingface.co/netease-youdao/Confucius4-R2T2 and https://github.com/netease-youdao/Confucius4-R2T2.
items.tldr: Confucius4-R2T2 propose un modèle ASR streaming stable (sans révision des tokens) pour la transcription en temps réel, basé sur le concept de 'Longest Stable Prefix' (LSP) et post-entraînement de Qwen3-ASR-1.7B.

items.title: Sketchpad: certified exact arithmetic with a small vision-language model
items.summary: Language models are accurate on most long-arithmetic problems, but their accuracy is estimated on samples and carries no guarantee for an unseen input; tool use is exact but moves the computation outside the network. We show that exactness at all input lengths becomes a finite, checkable property of a network when each of its steps reads only a bounded view of an external working memory. In Sketchpad, Qwen3.5-0.8B with a low-rank adapter executes arithmetic procedures on a rendered sheet. Each forward pass reads a three-cell view and emits one step: a digit, a carry or borrow, and the next operation. A fixed runtime moves the view and writes no digit of a result. We prove in Lean that the model is then exact on all inputs of any length if and only if it is exact on the finite set of views the runtime presents, that no finite test suffices when steps also read earlier steps, and that the guarantee tolerates bounded numerical perturbation and extends to compositions of procedures. All 2,446 views pass on the deployment device, a laptop GPU running the model in a web browser. The certified model performs signed addition and subtraction, long multiplication and division, square roots and greatest common divisors at arbitrary length. It solved 200 of 200 pre-registered problems in the browser, and 220 of 220 sums of up to 1,000 digits and products of up to 20 digits, of which GPT-6.1 Sol, the strongest of ten other models, solved 217. A symbolic runtime built on these procedures solves, expands and factors polynomials with every number computed by the model, and a multiplicative gate on the adapter recovers the base model exactly when the sheet is not in use.
items.tldr: Sketchpad utilise un petit modèle vision-langage (Qwen3.5-0.8B) avec un adaptateur basse-rang pour effectuer des calculs arithmétiques exacts certifiés via une mémoire externe bornée, garantissant l'exactitude sur tous les entrées.

items.title: Learning to evolve by matching velocities
items.summary: Learning the continuous-time evolution of nonlinear dynamical systems relies on trajectory-based objectives, which require simulating the learned dynamics during training and backpropagating through the numerical scheme, at a cost that grows with the rollout horizon. We show that trajectory-based objectives degenerate as the rollout horizon increases, hindering gradient-based optimization, and that the numerical scheme biases the learned dynamics by constraining the spectrum of the learned Jacobian to its absolute stability region. To overcome these limitations, we introduce Velocity Matching (VM), a simulation-free objective that relies on piecewise-linear interpolation and stochastic collocation, and approximates the velocity population risk to second order in the sampling step. We develop a theoretical framework for velocity-based learning, introducing stability estimates that control trajectory errors in terms of velocity errors, which enable us to establish universal and continuous-time approximation results when the learned velocity field is parameterized by deep neural networks. Building on a bias-variance decomposition of the VM objective, we show that its higher-order approximation of the velocity population risk yields a consistent minimizer; that it relates to the residual of an A-stable continuous-stage Runge-Kutta scheme, thus connecting VM to implicit integration without requiring any implicit solve; and that it implicitly matches the action of the learned Jacobian to that of the true one along the observed trajectories, without requiring access to the underlying velocity field or its Jacobian. Numerical experiments on nonlinear ordinary differential equations and semi-discretized time-dependent partial differential equations show that VM improves accuracy over trajectory-based objectives, while avoiding both the cost of simulation and the instabilities of long rollouts.
items.tldr: Velocity Matching (VM) introduit un objectif sans simulation pour apprendre l'évolution de systèmes dynamiques non linéaires, évitant les biais des schémas numériques et les problèmes de dégénérescence des objectifs basés sur trajectoires. Une analyse théorique et des résultats empiriques valident son efficacité.

items.title: Static Recovery Is Not Dynamic Stability: Dynamics-Aware Benchmarking of Protein Motif Scaffolding
items.summary: Protein motif scaffolding benchmarks assess whether generative models can build scaffolds around functionally important residues. Their conclusions depend on which motifs are tested and which criteria define success. Existing benchmarks typically use small hand-curated motif sets and static refolding criteria, but protein function often depends on conformational ensembles and transitions. Here, we address both benchmark scope and success criteria. We introduce BILBY-PRO, a systematically derived benchmark of structurally conserved functional motifs from PROSITE-linked experimental structures, comprising 220 cases from 174 PROSITE motif-pattern entries. Evaluating six recent scaffold-generation models reveals distinct patterns in target coverage and unique-solution yield: RFDiffusion and Proteina solve more targets, whereas ESM3 produces more unique successful scaffolds on the targets it solves. We further introduce BILBY-MD, a reference-based all-atom molecular dynamics evaluation framework. Applied to statically solved designs from the original MotifBench benchmark, it compares motif drift, scaffold drift, motif-contact preservation, and motif-dihedral free-energy landscapes against reference simulations. Of 55 statically solved model-problem pairs, 31 satisfy our MD-supported criterion and only 8 pass all checks. Compact, self-contained motifs are often MD-supported, whereas interface-like or context-dependent motifs fail more frequently. Static refolding success therefore provides useful evidence of local motif recovery but does not establish dynamical fidelity of the full scaffold. BILBY highlights three complementary axes of motif-scaffolding evaluation: target coverage, unique-solution yield, and MD-supported dynamical fidelity.
items.tldr: BILBY-PRO et BILBY-MD proposent un benchmark systématique et une évaluation dynamique (MD) pour le *protein motif scaffolding*, révélant des limites des critères statiques et des différences de performance entre modèles (RFDiffusion, ESM3).

items.title: "PRISM" Is Not All You Need: Cross-Topic Name Collisions and Scientific Paper Retrieval
items.summary: Scientific names increasingly connect papers from different research topics, leaving readers to recover a paper's identity from context. We study this convergence in 564,861 AI-related arXiv records. Cross-topic name collision grows 4.33-fold from a pooled 2020-2022 reference to 2026, compared with 1.12-fold within topics. A second sentence encoder reproduces the pattern, and name-group resampling quantifies its uncertainty. Fixed word-frequency bands locate the main increase in an intermediate-frequency vocabulary shared by many research areas. We then measure the ambiguity that remains after supplying research clues. With the same three-term query construction, shared-name targets retain matched identification deficits of 25.7 percentage points under title-based BM25 and 6.9 points under title-plus-abstract E5. Within fixed same-name candidates, listwise language-model ranking reaches 89.2% using the query and candidate titles. Topic-specific comparisons show that context resolves more cross-topic ambiguity. The evaluation separates candidate competition, document fields, and contextual ranking through lexical, dense, and language-model baselines. Source-linked cases and a portable evaluation collection make the phenomenon inspectable and reusable for scientific retrieval and research assistants.
items.tldr: Cette étude quantifie les collisions de noms entre topics dans les publications IA (x4.33 depuis 2020), montrant que les modèles de retrieval (BM25, E5) peinent à désambiguïser les cibles partageant des noms, même avec des indices contextuels.

items.title: Show HN: Flide: Make Jev-like decision models up to 9.5x faster
items.tldr: Outil open-source (Flide) revendiquant une accélération jusqu'à 9.5x pour des modèles de décision, potentiellement lié à l'optimisation d'inférence, mais manque de détails techniques ou de benchmarks.

items.title: N1nEmAn/sapper-v2
items.summary: Autonomous pentest legion — AI commander + worker swarm + layered fact-intent graph. 3rd Tencent Intelligent Attack-Defense online champion (634 teams · 8h unattended · 1B tokens beat 4.5B). The Nüwa Test: give AIs Create/Language/History, let a civilization grow.
items.tldr: Framework open-source (Sapper-v2) pour des tests d'attaque autonome par IA, avec des claims de performance (1B tokens vs 4.5B) mais manque de transparence méthodologique ou de peer-review.
